title: The ancient Olympic Games
examples: What were the main events at the ancient Olympics?
How did the ancient Olympics connect to the modern ones?
Why did the ancient Greeks hold these games?

explain.say: Today we learn about the ancient Olympic Games. These games were held in a place called Olympia. Olympia was a sacred site for the ancient Greeks.
The ancient games are traditionally believed to have started in seven hundred seventy-six before common era. This date marks the beginning of the recorded games.
The events included athletic contests and dramatic performances. For example, the running race called the stadion was a major event.
The ancient games were held every four years. This cycle was significant to the Greek calendar and culture.
The modern Olympics revived the spirit of the ancient games. They are held in different cities around the world today.
In real life, the Olympics spirit is seen in school sports days. Students compete in various events to show skill and teamwork.

faq.q: When did the ancient Olympic Games first take place?
faq.a: They are traditionally believed to have begun in seven hundred seventy-six before common era. This date marks the start of the recorded athletic competitions.
asks: What is the starting date for the games?

faq.q: What kind of events were part of the ancient games?
faq.a: The events included running races, wrestling, and other physical contests. These showcased the physical prowess of the athletes.

faq.q: Are the modern Olympics the same as the ancient ones?
faq.a: They share the spirit of competition but are much larger and held in different modern cities. The modern games include many more sports.
asks: Are the modern games exactly like the old ones?
What is the connection between the two?

faq.q: Why were the games held in Olympia?
faq.a: Olympia was considered a sacred site for the ancient Greeks. The games were part of religious festivals honoring the gods.
asks: Why was that specific location chosen?

faq.q: Did the ancient games happen every year?
faq.a: No, the ancient games were held every four years. This four-year cycle was known as an Olympiad.
asks: How often were the games held?
What was the time gap between games?

facts: The ancient games were held in Olympia, Greece.
The first recorded date is 776 before common era.
Events included running, wrestling, and pankration.
The games were held every four years.

quiz.say: The ancient games were held in which sacred location?
quiz.why: Olympia was the specific sacred site where the ancient games took place.

wrong.0: Rome was a later empire; the ancient games predated its main influence.
wrong.2: Athens was a major Greek city, but not the primary site for the ancient Olympics.
wrong.3: Sparta was famous for its military strength, but the games were held elsewhere.

quiz.say: What was the approximate starting date of the ancient games?
quiz.why: This date is the traditionally accepted start year for the recorded games.

wrong.0: This date is incorrect; the start date is significantly earlier.
wrong.2: This date is too recent; the games started much earlier.
wrong.3: One after common era is too late for the ancient contests.

quiz.say: If the games were held in year X, in what year would the next games be expected?
quiz.why: The games followed a regular four-year cycle, known as an Olympiad.

wrong.1: Holding them every year would be too frequent for the ancient schedule.
wrong.2: The cycle was much shorter than ten years.
wrong.3: The gap was fixed at four years, not just skipping one year.
